subject: PrivateCP: assertion policy reconciliation and SCIM provisioning gaps
messages:
From: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@acme-ops.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateCP - user provisioning mismatches and unexpected role drops

Hi Naomi,

We noticed intermittent failures where users that sign in via our IdP (Okta) get created in the Private control plane but are missing the expected "engineering" role. The error in the SCIM logs shows a 400 on PATCH /Users/{id} - "invalid attribute: roles".

Quick summary of what we see:
- SAML assertion from Okta contains attributes: eduPersonPrincipalName, mail, groups, title, employeeType.
- The assertion includes group names like "acme_priv_redwood_engineering" and also a shorter "redwood-eng" for some accounts.
- On creation the SCIM object sometimes has no roles attribute; provisioning sends group -> role mapping, but our mapping service returns empty for the short names.

We attached a CSV (privcp-assertion-mapping-diff.csv) with 30 examples. Can Redwood confirm whether the Private control plane is performing any canonicalization of SAML attributes (lowercasing, trimming, domain slicing) before mapping groups to RBAC roles? Also would appreciate the recommended fallback behavior so we don't leave users without access during cutover.

Thanks,
Alice
--
Alice Cheng
Identity & IAM Lead, Acme Operations
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@acme-ops.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateCP - user provisioning mismatches and unexpected role drops

Alice — thanks for the clear examples, that CSV helped. Short answer: the Private Control Plane (privatecp) has two places that touch assertions: the ingestion layer (where we canonicalize SAML attributes) and the provisioning adapter (which maps groups -> roles and submits SCIM). Right now canonicalization is fairly conservative and only lowercases the group + strips whitespace; it does NOT remove suffixes/prefixes or split by delimiters. That explains why "acme_priv_redwood_engineering" maps correctly (exact match) but "redwood-eng" does not.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Add a policy layer that applies regex-based normalization to groups before mapping. Example rules: lower-case, remove common prefixes (acme_priv_, acme-priv-), normalize delimiters (dots, underscores, hyphens -> dash), and expand common aliases (redwood-eng -> redwood-engineering).
2) Provision a temporary fallback role assignment: if group mapping returns empty, assign a restricted "pending-access" role and send an automated ticket to Acme IT + Redwood eng for manual review.
3) Add a one-shot reconciliation job that re-runs mapping for recently created users (last 72h) and applies corrective PATCHes.

Longer-term: make the mapping rules declarative in the customer's Private control plane config (so you can add alias rules yourself).

Action items I propose:
- Redwood to ship a normalization prototype + role fallback by 2027-07-02 EOD (we can run it in canary for your tenant).
- Acme to provide a short list of group alias patterns and a sample of 10 target accounts that should be "engineering" but are not (so we can validate).

I'll loop Marcus on the runtime implications (he's our provisioning lead).

Best,
Naomi
--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@acme-ops.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateCP - user provisioning mismatches and unexpected role drops

Thanks Naomi / Alice — digging into the provisioning logs I can add some implementation detail: our mapping engine performs a map lookup against the tenant's role-mapping table (keyed by exact group string). If the key is missing we currently log and skip (hence the missing "roles" attribute). The SCIM client then sends a PATCH with an empty roles array, which Okta rejects in some cases (depending on the content-type).

Notes from my investigation:
- The SCIM library we use treats missing/empty roles heterogeneously across downstream systems; we should normalize to either omit the roles attribute entirely or supply an explicit null/placeholder; currently we sometimes send [] and sometimes omit the element.
- Making the mapping tolerant (regex/alias) is cheap CPU-wise; the risk is creating accidental privilege (false positive matches). To mitigate we should require a second confirmation signal or default to the "pending-access" role as Naomi suggested.

Implementation plan (short):
A) Normalize input: lower-case + replace [._] with '-' + trim known prefixes/suffixes. Regex config stored in tenant config.
B) If no match: set roles=["pending-access"] and emit a reconciliation task id in the audit_log.
C) Re-run reconciliation for last 72h users as a background job (idempotent).

I'll prepare a small patch to the mapping engine and the SCIM client to consistently omit roles when we explicitly want no assignment. Target: 2027-07-02 for canary.

Attachment: role-mapping-regex.txt (examples of suggested regex replacements).

-marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Provisioning & Integrations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrivateCP - user provisioning mismatches and unexpected role drops

Hi all,

Thanks — that approach sounds good. A couple of clarifying questions from our IdP side:
- If Redwood normalizes groups, will you persist the original raw group value on the SCIM user object (audit) so we can trace back?
- For the fallback "pending-access" role, can we control the TTL/expiration? We prefer auto-expire after 7 days unless an admin confirms.

We attached our short alias list and an export of the 10 target accounts (CSV). We're OK with a canary run on a subset of users if that simplifies validation.

Alice
--
Alice Cheng
Identity & IAM Lead, Acme Operations
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Cheng <alice.cheng@acme-ops.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-02T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivateCP - assertion policy reconciliation and SCIM provisioning gaps

Alice — quick status update and next steps after internal sync:

1) We will persist a new field on the tenant's audit record called assertion_raw_groups (array of strings) that contains the SAML Group attribute exactly as received. This will be visible in the PrivateCP audit logs (immutable) so you can trace mapping decisions.
2) The fallback role will be created as a tenant-scoped role named "pending-access". TTL will be configurable; default will be 7 days and we will set TTL=7d in the canary. After TTL expires the role will be removed automatically and an admin notification will be emitted.
3) We will push the normalization + mapping changes to canary on 2027-07-02 22:00 UTC for Acme tenant only. The reconciliation job will run immediately after canary deploy and process the last 7 days of user creations.

Deliverables we will provide to Acme:
- scim-provisioning-playbook.pdf (runbook for operators; includes rollback steps).
- A one-line webhook (event) that your IdP can subscribe to for any users assigned "pending-access" so you can confirm or escalate.
- ACL change log entries and the reconciliation job id for audit (INF-2147).

Please reply here with the 10 account samples you attached or confirm you already shared the CSV; we'll start the canary once we have that.

Naomi
--
Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
